proposals.thesis: Airbnb offers the strongest researched continuation case: its issuer release reports Q3 revenue growth of 19%, Nights and Seats Booked growth of 16%, and a raised annual outlook. The SEC filing corroborates operating growth and Nasdaq Class A common-stock registration. The horizon bridge is modest continued reassessment of newly disclosed acceleration during November 9–13, rather than an established new operating catalyst. Friday's strong price response supports attention but also raises exhaustion risk. No within-week demand test is established, so the price forecast stands separately from the business thesis. The $12 billion additional repurchase authorization is optional capacity, not evidence of purchases this week.

scorecards.assessment: Primary issuer and SEC evidence supported operating acceleration, and discovery exclusions were reasoned. The proposal distinguished historical fundamentals from weekly demand and acknowledged exhaustion risk. Its positive forecast missed, and entry-price sensitivity remained qualitative despite a materially higher actual entry. The loss alone does not invalidate the research process.

forecast_comparisons: Researcher A forecast +1.2%, 54% probability of profit and a -7% adverse scenario. The matched execution-observation window returned -4.74% gross and -4.83% after costs. Positive continuation failed; the adverse scenario was not exceeded. Its historical $189.99 reference was not the actual entry.

Researcher B forecast +1.5% from $196.35, with a $199.30 expected endpoint, 53% profit probability and -10% adverse scenario. The $186.52 endpoint was approximately -5.01% from that research anchor and $12.78 below the expected endpoint. The realized one-share net return was -4.83%; the adverse scenario was not exceeded.

The exit observation exceeded the $184.05 structural floor but fell below $192.50 extension resistance. It was an intraday observation, so it cannot establish completed-close checkpoint outcomes. Structural survival would not validate either positive weekly forecast.

The decline contradicts immediate earnings continuation, while leaving the historical revenue, bookings and outlook disclosures intact. Neither the decline nor the recorded prices identify the cause of the reversal or calibrate the stated probabilities.
review.selected_vs_rejected: Selected B and rejected A proposed the same stock for the same week. At identical one-share execution prices, either proposal would have produced the same -$9.471160 result; selecting B did not demonstrate realized return superiority. B supplied a clearer current-price anchor and higher-entry scenario, supporting the manager's process preference. Rejecting A avoided duplicate exposure: after B's budget, the remaining 15% ticker allowance could not afford another share. Both forecasts missed the common declining window. Other discovery leads have no comparable entry-to-exit prices in these records, so their rejection cannot be judged by realized performance.
review.execution_effects: One simulated share bought at raw $195.80 filled at $195.897900; sale at raw $186.52 filled at $186.426740. The configured 2 bps spread plus 3 bps slippage per side cost $0.191160 total; fees were zero. Raw price movement lost $9.28, producing net loss $9.471160. Buy and sell cash movements reconcile to ending equity $981.32819835, displayed as $981.33. Execution followed the recorded model; these observations do not establish live executable prices.

review.limitations: This is one selected stock and two overlapping forecasts, a small sample with substantial hindsight limitations. Recent summaries add context but do not supply independent calibration or matched alternative prices. The supplied observations do not establish each completed daily-close checkpoint, a holding-week operating-demand change or causal attribution for the decline. Benchmark-relative performance cannot be calculated from an exit-only benchmark price. Scores assess documented process, not calibrated skill.

patches.text: For continuation proposals, pair expected return with an explicit reference price and an approximate expected endpoint or endpoint range. Recompute implied return at the latest supported observation and a higher-entry scenario. Researcher B demonstrated this distinction; A acknowledged higher-entry risk without quantifying it. Label these subjective scenarios and distinguish research prices from simulated fills.
patches.expected_effect: Make the modest estimated edge assessable when the entry moves materially beyond the historical reference.
patches.success_metric: For the next four applicable proposals, record the forecast anchor and show implied return at the latest supported price and one higher-entry scenario.
patches.rollback_condition: Retire if endpoint precision becomes misleading; retain explicit anchor and entry-sensitivity disclosure.

patches.text: Preserve the existing separation between structure, closing extension and holding-window profit. When proposing daily-close checkpoints, specify the dated completed-close evidence needed to assess them and label unassessed checkpoints explicitly. This cycle's $186.52 exit observation cannot resolve the proposed daily-close sequence. This is a research documentation trial, not an exit rule.
patches.expected_effect: Improve later assessment of structural retention and extension without confusing an intraday endpoint with a completed close.
patches.success_metric: Next four applicable proposals specify timestamped completed-close evidence for each checkpoint; subsequent reviews mark each as confirmed, breached or unassessed.
patches.rollback_condition: Retire if checkpoint documentation adds no interpretive value across four applicable reviews or encourages treating checkpoints as execution instructions.

runs.research_summary: Ran targeted live searches for the November 9–13 earnings calendar, recent guidance changes, earnings reactions, industrial/logistics opportunities, healthcare, power, semiconductor suppliers and NYSE American issuers. Opened issuer releases, an SEC operating filing, historical observations and timestamped reporting. Coverage was selective, not exhaustive. Compared smaller-company leads including REI and CECO, mid-sized industrial GXO, and larger technology/travel issuers; share price was not used as a market-cap proxy. ABNB's fresh operating acceleration plus a documented earnings response produced the clearest, though modest, weekly directional case. GXO had 6.4% organic growth but flat adjusted EBITDA, lower cash generation and its investor day outside the window. CSCO and AMAT have within-window earnings timing, but timing alone did not establish favorable surprises; CSCO's historical growth did not resolve expectations. REI's approximately $1.11 historical close fails the $5 floor. CECO's issuer site flagged a listing transfer, leaving exchange eligibility unresolved. GFS/VTRS/BWXT/VST were discovery leads without a stronger fully corroborated weekly setup; DKNG's reported guidance cut and CRWV's event risk weakened their comparisons. Submitted one finalist rather than force three. Two primary sources support ABNB. Historical daily data show more than 20 sessions and substantial volume, but no fresh cutoff-valid engine quote exists. Undated historical pages have null publication timestamps: only dated observations preceding cutoff are used, and retrospective revision remains possible. No subsequent earnings outcomes or unverified same-day previews were used. All allocation and execution checks remain binding.

Discovery included smaller-company opportunities alongside larger issuers across travel, defense, solar infrastructure, photonics, uranium, software and semiconductors; this was not exhaustive market coverage or a verified market-cap ranking. ABNB was the strongest adequately documented finalist. KRMN had strong reported growth but a 42.13% session jump created substantially greater extension risk. ARRY's merger announcement complicated a standalone continuation forecast. COHR's rebound followed a larger earnings-session decline and did not restore its pre-release close. UEC's rebound remained within a pronounced monthly decline. THM and GOGO were below $5 in discovery observations; AMD's $449.04 reference exceeded the approximately $396.32 ticker cap even for one share.
